description: Hi! Astrophysics student leading "Planet X and SPHEREx". The physics backend (Python/Astropy) is done. I need creative minds to visualize this massive near infrared sky data. Seeking: Web Developer/UI Design, storytelling. Want a NASA project on your resume without doing heavy maths or tedious physics equations? Let's build!
summary:
We built ExoMapper a web app that helps people hunt for hidden planets like Planet X.
Beyond Neptune scientists think a giant nine planet might be hiding and finding it is super hard because it is very cold and looks like a tiny dot that moves slowly over six months. To solve this we created a fun, easy to use browser game using python and streamlit.
With ExoMapper anyone can use real public data from NASA's SPHEREx telescope and IRSA archives. Our app lets player flips back and forth between two or more pictures of the same sky to spot moving dots, subtract background stars and even listen to space sound using Doppler waves.
This project is important because it lets students and space fans all over the world helps scientists look for new worlds right from their web browsers making real space science open and fun for everyone.
details:
Hello, we are team ExoMapper and we are so excited to share a fun, web based astronomy app that we built to help people search for hidden planets like Planet X right from the internet browser.

What does it do or how does it work?

Scientists believe there might be a giant ninth planet hiding far beyond Neptune in our solar system, finding it is extremely difficult because it is a super cold, very faint and moves slowly across the sky over many months and to make this easier we created an interactive observatory game. Players can upload or select two pictures of the exact same star field taken months apart. By using our Blink Comparator (which flips back and forth between the pictures) or our Dark Subtraction Map stationary background stars vanish and any moving object instantly pops right out. We also added a magnifying loupe, a tool to draw and check star coordinates and a fun Doppler sound feature that turns space motion into audio waves.

What benefits and impact does it have?

Space science and discovery should be open to everyone with this motto we wanted to remove all the complicated barriers so that students, teachers, and space fans all over the world can explore real NASA data instantly. Players can track their discoveries on a live scoreboard, download clean FITS files, and save CSV discovery logs. Our biggest hope is to inspire young learners everywhere to look up at the night sky and realize that they too can be citizen scientists helping to expand human knowledge.

What tools, languages, and software did we use?

We built ExoMapper using Python and Streamlit along with NumPy, Pandas, PIL, HTML5, and JavaScript. We connected our app directly to public data from NASA’s SPHEREx mission and the Infrared Science Archive (IRSA).

We drove the core vision, scientific concepts, astrometric formulas, and user experience for ExoMapper. We used Super Intelligence (AI) tools as a helpful copilot and development accelerator for writing and debugging our Python/Streamlit code, structuring our HTML5 canvas workflows, brainstorming Doppler sonification logic, and creating conceptual space background graphics.

All NASA branding elements remain strictly untouched, and full AI accountability notes are explicitly declared in our repository README.

How is it creative and what factors did our team consider?

We wanted our app to feel like a real professional telescope room while staying super welcoming and easy to use. Creativity for us meant blending hardcore astrophysics with genuine engagement we carefully considered data accessibility, performance optimization and cross platform design ensuring the interface runs smoothly across mobile phones, tablets, laptops, and large monitors with zero login barriers or software installation required or any hassle.

Anyone can open our live app (https://exomapper.streamlit.app/ ) or check out our open-source code on GitHub (https://github.com/Shikshita55/ExoMapper ) anytime.

let's keep looking up and find Planet X together.
